uncertain.main_blocker: Two caveats compete. (1) There is no free tier: dev access is a 30-day trial (about $400 of usage per Snowflake search snippets; the trial docs page gives no figure), then a paid account. (2) There is no global OAuth app. Each customer account's ACCOUNTADMIN must CREATE SECURITY INTEGRATION to register the client, which is per-tenant admin setup rather than vendor app review. I chose paid_plan; 'other' (per-account admin OAuth setup) is also defensible.
uncertain.auth_primary: OAuth2 is the natural multi-user choice, but it needs a per-account security integration. PAT or key-pair JWT is simpler for single-account setups.
uncertain.access: self_serve_trial per the trial page. Every real user of a toolkit is already a paying Snowflake customer, so for end users access is effectively paid.

notes: API surface: the SQL API (submit and poll arbitrary SQL statements) plus the Snowflake REST APIs for resource management (about 40 resource types: databases, schemas, tables, warehouses, users, roles, grants, tasks, stages, pipes, Cortex Search/Inference, etc.), alongside many drivers and SDKs. The vendor MCP is the 'Snowflake-managed MCP server': GA Nov 4, 2025 per release notes in search results, preview since Oct 2, 2025. It is a per-account object created with CREATE MCP SERVER and served from the account URL, so it is vendor-hosted but has no single global endpoint. It serves Cortex Analyst, Cortex Search, Cortex Agents, custom tools and SQL execution. The older local Snowflake-Labs/mcp repo is now archived on GitHub (archived=true per the GitHub API).
